notes: N-SCALING (Stage 2) IN PROGRESS. Tests generic-adherence (last pre-registered hypothesis). Pool: A(consolidate)/B(best-of-breed)/C(cheapest)/D(open-source), disjoint cues; held-out P_never = docs/community (band cue), never trained. Train first-N jointly at overlap 0; measure per-principal niche (partition) + held-out deference (generic-adherence). N in {2,3,4} x2 seeds. Files: src/slc/nscaling.py, configs/nscale.yaml, modal nscale_gen/nscale_cell/nscale_sweep, /data/nscale.

Rationale for choosing N-scaling over multi-principal Petri: multi-principal Petri is floor-bound (single-principal already dodges completely 1/10, so 'harder to audit' is un-measurable as a differential until an audit regime where single is detectable exists). N-scaling is directly testable, completes the pre-registered hypothesis set, and PRODUCES the N-principal organisms a future multi-principal Petri would need.
PETRI DONE: dodges under default + detection-tuned scoring; positive control validates; evades by never activating. All prior phases done (see outputs_*.csv + vault note). Budget uncapped per user.
User owns some Phase-3 scaffolding on remote (held-out queries, arm-based _evaluate); I rebase-before-push each time to avoid collision.
